title: User Unaware of Data Processing
description: Parent may not be informed about how their registration data (email, password, govt ID, etc.) will be processed, stored, or shared by the Authentication Service post-registration.
assumptions: Assumes no clear privacy policy or consent mechanism is presented during registration.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Sensitive registration data (including govt ID and password) could be intercepted if the communication channel between Parent User and Authentication Service is not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Assumes TLS/SSL may not be enforced or could be misconfigured.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: Authentication Service may store sensitive registration data (passwords, govt ID) without adequate encryption or access controls, risking exposure in case of a breach.
assumptions: Assumes default storage practices may not follow security best practices.

title: Unnecessary user data disclosure
description: Authentication Service shares more user data than required for the parent's purpose, increasing exposure risk.
uncertainty_note: Node D.1.1 assumed based on common LINDDUN Pro structure; exact tree may vary.

title: Unencrypted data transmission
description: JWT and user data sent over insecure channel, risking interception by third parties.
uncertainty_note: Assumes no encryption is used; actual implementation may differ.

title: Parent user data misuse
description: Parent may use received data for purposes beyond authentication, e.g., profiling or unauthorized sharing.
uncertainty_note: Node Dd.1.2 inferred; Dd.1.1 (insecure storage) could also apply depending on context.

title: Interception of parent credentials during transmission
description: Parent's email and password sent over the network could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Network communication is not encrypted or uses weak encryption.

title: Insecure storage of parent credentials
description: Authentication service may store parent's password without encryption, risking exposure if the database is compromised.
assumptions: Service stores credentials in plaintext or with weak hashing.

title: Linking child's account to parent's identity
description: Using parent's email for child's login creates a link between the child's activities and the parent's identity, potentially exposing the parent's data.
assumptions: Parent's email is used as a unique identifier for the child's account.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Child profile data (including government ID) could be intercepted during transmission from parent to profile management system.

title: Data used beyond original purpose
description: Child profile data may be used for purposes beyond profile management, such as marketing or third-party sharing.

title: Unique identification of child
description: Government ID and personal details allow unique identification of the child, increasing re-identification risk.

title: Non-compliance with data minimization
description: Parent may be compelled to provide government ID which may not be necessary for profile creation, violating data protection principles.
uncertainty_note: Assumes government ID collection is not legally required for this context.

title: Processing child's data without valid consent
description: Video Management Service processes child's data (search, likes, comments) without obtaining parental consent, violating regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K.

title: Unencrypted data transmission
description: Video search requests, likes, and comments are transmitted without encryption, risking interception by third parties.

title: Linking user activities to profile
description: Service links child's search history, likes, and comments to build a detailed user profile, enabling tracking across sessions.

title: Data used beyond original purpose
description: Child's interaction data is used for targeted advertising or third-party sharing without explicit consent.

title: Exposure of child's identity
description: Comments or profile data may contain personally identifiable information, leading to direct identification of the child.

title: Lack of transparency in data processing
description: Child and parents are not adequately informed about how their data is collected, used, and shared.

title: Data at rest not encrypted
description: Video metadata and files stored in MongoDB without encryption, risking exposure if the datastore is compromised.

title: Data contains PII
description: Metadata includes personally identifiable information (e.g., user IDs, timestamps) that could be used to identify individuals.

title: Unauthorized access to data
description: Insufficient access controls on MongoDB allow unauthorized personnel to access video data.

title: Lack of user awareness
description: Users are not informed that their video data is being stored, leading to lack of consent.

title: Non-compliance with legal requirements
description: Storing video data may violate regulations like GDPR if retention policies or consent mechanisms are not followed.

title: Data in transit intercepted
description: Video data transmitted between P2 and DS3 without encryption, risking interception.

title: Direct identification of child via profile data
description: Child profile data sent to datastore includes unique identifiers (e.g., child ID), enabling direct identification of the child.
assumptions: Data includes persistent identifiers linked to the child.

title: Unencrypted data transmission
description: Child search/watch history data transmitted without encryption, risking interception by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data flow lacks transport-layer encryption.

title: Secondary use of stored child data
description: Stored child history data may be accessed or repurposed beyond profile management (e.g., marketing, third-party sharing).
assumptions: Datastore access controls or usage policies are insufficient.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Storing child search/watch history may violate regulations (e.g., COPPA) if consent, data minimization, or safeguards are inadequate.
assumptions: System lacks explicit parental consent or age-appropriate privacy controls.

title: Lack of transparency in data collection
description: Children/guardians may not be adequately informed about collection/storage of search/watch history.
assumptions: Privacy notices or consent mechanisms are unclear or absent.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Child browsing data transmitted from MongoDB to AI engine may be intercepted if not encrypted, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Data in transit lacks encryption or secure channel.

title: Unauthorized Secondary Use of Data
description: AI engine may process child browsing data for purposes beyond recommendations (e.g., profiling, advertising) without explicit consent.
assumptions: AI engine has broad data access without strict purpose limitation.

title: Re-identification of Children
description: AI engine could link anonymized browsing data to specific children using auxiliary data, compromising identifiability.
assumptions: Data is not sufficiently anonymized or AI has access to linking datasets.

title: Lack of Transparency in Data Usage
description: Children/parents may be unaware their browsing data is used for AI-driven recommendations, violating informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly disclose AI processing purposes.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: AI processing of child data may violate laws like COPPA/GDPR-K if consent, data minimization, or retention rules are not followed.
assumptions: Legal requirements for child data processing are not fully implemented.

title: Data contains direct identifiers
description: Browsing data includes cookies, device IDs, or other identifiers that can directly identify users.
assumptions: Browsing data transmitted includes persistent identifiers.

title: Data intercepted during transmission
description: Unencrypted browsing data in transit could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without end-to-end encryption.

title: Data used for unauthorized profiling
description: Advertisers may use browsing data to create user profiles beyond the original consent scope or intended purpose.
assumptions: Advertisers process data for purposes not explicitly agreed upon by users.

title: Unauthorized disclosure by Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service may transmit government ID images to the File System without verifying user consent or proper authorization, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit user consent or authorization checks are performed before data sharing.

title: Unencrypted transmission of government ID images
description: The data flow lacks encryption, allowing potential interception of sensitive government ID images during transmission between the Authentication Service and File System.
assumptions: Assumes no transport-layer encryption (e.g., TLS) is implemented for this data flow.

title: Insecure storage of government ID images
description: The File System may not implement sufficient access controls or encryption at rest, leading to unauthorized access to stored government ID images.
assumptions: Assumes no role-based access controls or encryption for stored data.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Storing government ID images without a proper legal basis or adherence to data minimization principles may violate regulations like GDPR or local privacy laws.
assumptions: Assumes no documented legal basis or retention policy for storing government ID images.

title: JWT exposed via XSS leading to unauthorized access
description: Storing JWT in localStorage allows malicious scripts to access the token, enabling session hijacking and unauthorized data access.
assumptions: Assumes potential XSS vulnerabilities in the browser environment.

title: Unintended disclosure of child history data
description: Process P3 may share more child history data than necessary for parent review, leading to unintended disclosure of sensitive information.
assumptions: Data minimization controls are not enforced

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Child history data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: No encryption is used for data in transit

title: Data misuse by parent user
description: Parent may use child's history data for purposes beyond review, such as sharing with third parties or non-consensual profiling.
assumptions: No technical or policy controls restrict data usage post-receipt
